sections.label: Girl Effect income reinvestment
sections.summary: The 2009 World Economic Forum's Girl Effect noted women and girls reinvest 90% of income into families, versus 30% to 40% for men.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The "Girl Effect" that was highlighted in the World Economic Forum 2009, for instance, noted that women and girls with income reinvest 90% of it into their families, as compared to about 30% to 40% for men.

sections.label: Women undergraduates in Singapore
sections.summary: More than 50% of undergraduates in Singapore are women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: More than 50% of undergraduates in Singapore are women.

sections.label: Gender parity gaps and timeline
sections.summary: The system has gaps, including women's under-representation at higher workforce levels, and parity may take 50 or 170 years naturally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But we also need to acknowledge the gaps and weaknesses in our system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We need to take action to accelerate our progression towards gender parity, or we will have to wait at least 50 years according to Accenture, or 170 years according to the World Economic Forum, if we are to leave things to evolve naturally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: One key gap is the gender imbalance in our workforce, where women tend to be under-represented at the higher levels.

sections.label: SkillsFuture package for back-to-work women
sections.summary: A SkillsFuture package for back-to-work women should have capability development, job matching and interim financial support, and eldercare could use retired nurses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The same can, of course, be extended to those who need eldercare help and services, for instance, a network of retired nurses engaged and deployed to conduct home care for our elders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We need to develop a SkillsFuture package dedicated to help "back-to-work women", to rebuild confidence, to refresh skills or acquire new ones, and facilitate their transition back to the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I would suggest three components critical to the success of this package, namely, capability development, job matching and interim financial support.

sections.label: Subsistence allowances and flexible work
sections.summary: The package should provide subsistence allowances or training grants, and flexible work arrangements should be accelerated so Singaporeans can pursue family and career.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Many caregivers have sacrificed their prime years and savings to care for their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, even as they get trained for prospective employment, they might need some help with living expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, the package should also provide subsistence allowances or training grants to see them through their training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We also need to accelerate implementation of flexible work arrangements (FWAs) so that Singaporeans have the option to achieve both family and career aspirations without having to trade off one for the other.

sections.label: Sector-specific FWA standards call
sections.summary: Building on the PAP Women's Wing recommendation, MOM is called on to implement industry- or sector-specific FWA standards alongside existing laws and guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As such, building on to our PAP Women's Wing recommendation last year, I would like to call on the Ministry for Manpower (MOM) to implement industry- or sector-specific FWA standards to complement the existing employment laws, tripartite guidelines and advisories.

sections.label: Women in workforce and boards
sections.summary: Women are half of entry-level workers but only 9.7% at board level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Women in Singapore start off well, comprising half of the workforce at the entry level but this proportion dwindles drastically as they journey up the career ladder, with women comprising a mere 9.7% at the board level.

sections.label: Call for female directors
sections.summary: Minister Grace Fu called for at least 20% female directors on boards by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Recently, Minister Grace Fu, on behalf of the PAP Women's Wing and BoardAgender, called for at least 20% female directors on boards by the year 2020.

sections.label: Digital fluency and gender gaps
sections.summary: A 2016 Accenture study says digital fluency can halve the time to close gender gaps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: According to a 2016 study report by Accenture, the time needed to close gender gaps can be halved if women are digitally fluent.

sections.label: SkillsFuture for back-to-work women
sections.summary: Stay-at-home mothers and daughters should be helped to be digitally fluent, starting with a SkillsFuture package.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But for now, we should also help our stay-at-home mothers and daughters to be digitally fluent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And we can start with the SkillsFuture package for Back-to-Work Women encompassing modules in IT literacy and basic programming.

sections.label: Women's share at board level
sections.summary: Women are half of entry-level workers but only 9.7% at board level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Women comprise half of the workforce at the entry level but this proportion dwindles drastically as they journey up the career ladder, with women comprising a mere 9.7% at the board level.

sections.label: Four angles to help women
sections.summary: Singaporean women should be helped through caregiver infrastructure, flexible work, valuing their contributions, and technology training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Every Singaporean should have the opportunity to enjoy family and career life at the same time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, we must help Singaporean women from four angles: first, establish and strengthen infrastructure and services to lighten the caregivers' burden, so that they can have time and better manage their multiple roles; second, promote FWA so that they can look after the family without sacrificing their career; third, encourage the society and the companies to value women's economic potentials and contributions; and fourth, encourage women to undergo technology and skills training and be prepared for the new digital era and the future economy.

sections.label: Supporting Singapore women's aspirations
sections.summary: The speaker says now is the best time to support Singapore women and affirms their familial, social and economic contributions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We believe that now is the best time as Singapore is transforming to be future-ready.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: There are many things we can do to support Singapore women, but even as we continue to co-create these solutions, I believe that it is important that this House affirms the familial, social and economic contributions of Singapore women and our support for them to fulfil their family and career aspirations and be future-ready.

sections.label: Training women in digital skills
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a plan to help women and girls build skills for the digital revolution, citing a gap in technology and STEM.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Just as the Minister had outlined a plan over the next few years for the Government Technology Agency (GovTech), in partnership with the National University of Singapore (NUS), to train 10,000 public officers in data science, with the current gap of women in technology in the workforce and in STEM education, we also need to drive a plan to enable women and girls to build the skills to be able to have the ability to ride this digital revolution.

sections.label: Female workforce participation rise
sections.summary: Female workforce participation rose from 57.7% in 2012 to 60.4% in 2016, still below male participation at 76.2%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Although still lagging male workforce participation at 76.2%, female workforce participation has increased from 57.7% in 2012 to 60.4% now in 2016.

sections.label: Gender pay gap in Singapore
sections.summary: The World Economic Forum Global Gender Report states pay for women in Singapore lags men for similar work at a ratio of 0.81.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Based on the World Economic Forum Global Gender Report, pay for women still lags behind that of men for similar work in Singapore at a ratio of 0.81.

sections.label: Women in senior business roles
sections.summary: The speaker says pay should be based on contributions not gender, and notes women in senior business roles rose to 30% from 26%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Pay should be based on contributions and not gender.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: It is encouraging that the proportion of senior business roles held by women in Singapore has also risen to 30% this year, up from 26% last year.

sections.label: Women on boards and C-Suite
sections.summary: The speaker says women's progress on boards and C-Suite needs attention, noting 9.7% on boards in 2016 and calls for 20% female directors by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Progress of the number of women, not just on boards, but on C-Suite positions, need attention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: And as Ms Tin Pei Ling had shared, the progress of women on boards listed in Singapore has been slow at only 9.7% in 2016, lagging many advanced countries and even behind countries in Asia like China, Hong Kong and India.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Two weeks ago, the PAP Women's Wing and BoardAgender have called for a revision to the Code of Corporate Governance to include a "comply or explain" disclosure policy for companies on their board diversity, including gender, in their annual reports and setting a target of at least of having 20% female directors on boards by 2020.

sections.label: Implicit Association Test preferences
sections.summary: A global Implicit Association Test study of over 200,000 participants found 64% preferred young people and 75% associated male with career, female with family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: According to a global online research study done by Implicit Association Test with over 200,000 participants, 64% of participants demonstrated a strong or moderate preference for young people as compared to old people; 75% of participants associated male with career, and female with family.

sections.label: Women as emerging market
sections.summary: EY states women's combined global income will reach about $18 trillion by 2018, but companies do not tap female talent, risking missed opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: According to EY (previously Ernst & Young), women are the new emerging market with a combined global income that will grow to approximately $18 trillion by 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: But research also reveals that although most companies look at women for end-users, they do not tap their female talent base to understand what women need.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: So, imagine this: if only males were making decisions on what innovations that companies will invest in, based on a thought process of their experience and on what products that they can use themselves, then, we have a serious problem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Not having gender diversity at all levels will see us missing out on huge opportunities; opportunities that could slow down both societal development and the economy.

sections.label: Re-engaging retired nurses
sections.summary: Retired nurses can be re-engaged on a casual hours basis as a segment to tap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A segment that we can tap on is that of the retired nurses, who can be re-engaged on a "casual hours" basis.

sections.label: Eldercare and women returner support
sections.summary: The passage proposes short-term eldercare accommodation, two days of eldercare leave annually, and course subsidies for women returning to work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Services at more of our eldercare centres can be augmented to include places for short-term accommodation for the elderly who need to stay there temporarily when their caregivers have to travel overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I would also like to take this opportunity to appeal again to the Government to legislate at least two days of eldercare leave per annum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to reiterate my request for additional course subsidies, on top of the SkillsFuture Credit, for women who wish to return to work after being out of the workforce for a number of years.

sections.label: CPF transfers for homemakers
sections.summary: The passage proposes mechanisms to encourage transferring up to 50% of husbands' monthly CPF contributions to homemakers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As a practical way of recognising the contributions of our homemakers, I would like to propose mechanisms to encourage up to 50% of their husbands' Central Provident Fund (CPF) monthly contributions be transferred to them.

sections.label: Median age of brides
sections.summary: A Department of Statistics report stated the median age of brides at first marriage rose from 26.9 years in 2005 to 28.2 years in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: A report by the Department of Statistics released about two weeks ago stated that the median age in the first marriage for brides rose from 26.9 years in 2005, to 28.2 years in 2015.

sections.label: ART subsidies age limit
sections.summary: ART subsidies are limited to women below 40 at public hospitals, with a case for reduced subsidies for those aged 41 to 42.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: While there are generous subsidies for ART, only women below 40 years old can benefit from it and, even then, the subsidies only apply for procedures at public hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: While the chances of conceiving drop after 40 and we should ensure public subsidies are well-targeted, there is a case to be made in having a reduced subsidy rate for those who are between 41 years old and 42 years old.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements for mothers
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Government gives new mothers a statutory right of FWA in the first year of childbirth, as implemented in the UK.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: They are in a dilemma and are not sure what to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can give the new mothers the statutory right of FWA within the first year of childbirth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This has been implemented in the UK for many years and was welcomed by women and employers alike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This can promote pro-family practices and work arrangements and is a booster for women who are currently agonising over balancing work and family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Singaporean women need comprehensive support to fulfil their aspirations in family and career life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The measures outlined in the Motion can help Singaporean women achieve their dreams and aspirations.

sections.label: Women's labour force participation rate
sections.summary: MOM statistics show women's LFPR was 60.4% in 2016, an increase from 54.3% in 2006.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Based on Ministry of Manpower's (MOM's) statistics, LFPR of women in 2016 was 60.4%.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: That is an increase compared to 54.3% in 2006.

sections.label: Reviewing the tuition industry
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to review the tuition industry and consider diverting its resources to public schools.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Does this contradict the efforts to drive a mindset change of enabling our children to learn broadly, discover and pursue their passion?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to begin reviewing the tuition industry before it becomes counter intuitive to our broader efforts in making fundamental changes in our education system.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Also, to consider whether resources from this tuition industry can be diverted to our public schools − enrichment classes in the school by private tutors to supplement the school teachers in catering for students weaker in specific subjects or guidance for their homework.

sections.label: Public and private sector FWAs
sections.summary: The public sector and some private companies can lead in enabling FWAs for functions suited to flexibility, helping women return to work.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The public sector and some private sector companies of different industries can take the lead in enabling FWAs for some of the functions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Those like the service-related, the backend office operations that can accommodate work location flexibility, shorter training cycles, leverage on technology; they should consider leveraging an existing pool of women and assist them to return to the workforce.

sections.label: MOM action on employment
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOM to take a tougher stance against such employment, including outsourcing companies hiring part-time older workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: A tougher stance, I would urge, is for MOM to take against such employment, including those outsourcing companies, particularly the ones that hire our part-time older workers.

sections.label: Subsidies for non-working mothers, singles' eldercare leave
sections.summary: Asks the Ministry to consider equal subsidised childcare rates for non-working mothers and eldercare leave or converted medical leave for singles.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: But we understand the reason why it is so.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Ministry to consider giving equal subsidised rate for the non-working mothers who are going to be gainfully employed after six months of placing their children at the childcare services.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Second, for the singles − to provide the eldercare leave or to allow them to convert the unused medical leave to care for their elderly at home.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: They do not have additional care leave to cater for the caring of their elderly at home.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: There are many reasons why people do not live under the same roof but living apart does not indicate that they provide less care for their parents.

sections.label: Support for single parents
sections.summary: States singles have fewer resources and proposes caregiving coaching and interim support for their children's first six years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Most of them would be working and, being single, inherently means they just have fewer resources, whether it is in terms of leave, childcare support and so on.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Thus, providing them with coaching on caregiving and any form of interim support for the first six years of their children's lives would be invaluable.

sections.label: Startup spaces in neighbourhoods
sections.summary: Proposes establishing startup spaces in neighbourhoods so women can work closer to home or part-time.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: First, establish the startup spaces in neighbourhoods to enable women to work closer to home or even on a part-time basis.

sections.label: Basic services close to home
sections.summary: Lists basic services near home such as meal catering, minding old folks, nanny services, home cleaning and laundry.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Some of the basic services that can be created very close to home could include essential caregiving that offer meals catering, minding of the old folks at home, nanny services, home cleaning, laundry and so on.

sections.label: Men sharing caregiving
sections.summary: States that men need to step up and hold their fair share.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Men need to step up and hold their fair share.

sections.label: Gender diversity in companies
sections.summary: Says companies should take concrete steps to advance greater gender diversity in all roles, including management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: From corporate boardrooms to the cockpits of airlines, companies should take concrete steps to advance greater gender diversity in all roles, including management roles.

sections.label: Part-time work and job sharing
sections.summary: The state can do more to promote flexibility in part-time work, job sharing and re-entry for women, with Civil Service such arrangements rising from about 1,500 in 2011 to about 2,000 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While progress has undoubtedly been made, the state can do more to promote greater flexibility in part-time work, job sharing and re-entry into the workforce for women who have taken a break for childcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I note the reply to my Parliamentary Question a few months ago on job sharing and part-time work in the Civil Service that those on such arrangements increased from about 1,500 in 2011 to about 2,000 in 2015.

sections.label: Fair Employment Contribution Fund proposal
sections.summary: Mr Faisal Manap last year called for a voluntary Fair Employment Contribution Fund to promote fair employment practices before possibly legislating anti-discrimination laws under a National Employment Framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My colleague Mr Faisal Manap last year called for a voluntary Fair Employment Contribution Fund to be created to promote fair employment practices as a precursor to possibly legislating anti-discrimination laws under a broader National Employment Framework.

sections.label: Equal pay for same work
sections.summary: Whether women are paid less for the same work as men needs addressing, as published data is inconclusive and a further study should be done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One area that needs to be addressed is whether women are being paid less for doing the same work as men.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The published data is inconclusive and a further study should be done.

sections.label: Housing access for single parents
sections.summary: More can be done to enhance benefits and access to housing for single parents, including unwed mothers, as WP Members have long argued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: More still can be done to enhance benefits and, in particular, access to housing for single parents, including unwed mothers, as WP Members have long argued for.

sections.label: Firms allowing permanent home working
sections.summary: Only 6.2% of firms allow their workers to work from home permanently.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, only 6.2% of firms allow their workers to work from home permanently.

sections.label: Productivity and turnover from flexi-work
sections.summary: A Stanford study found call centre workers increased productivity by 13% working from home, and MOM's report noted firms with more flexi-work have lower long-term turnover.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In one Stanford study, call centre workers increased their productivity by 13% when they worked from home.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the long term, firms with more flexi-work have lower turnover, as noted by MOM's report.

sections.label: CPF auto transfer for homemakers
sections.summary: The Government can allow auto transfer from a spouse's CPF once it reaches the full retirement sum, unless the spouse opts out.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, for older homemakers who cannot work much anymore, the Government can allow auto transfer from spouse's CPF when her spouse's CPF saving has reached full retirement sum unless her spouse opts out.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credits and CPF transfers
sections.summary: The Government can give more SkillsFuture credits or home-based courses, and CPF Board can transfer money from family members with sufficient CPF savings.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government can give them more SkillsFuture credits or offer more home-based courses.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Perhaps CPF Board can transfer a certain amount of money from their family members who have sufficient CPF savings.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If the Budget allows, the Government can consider offering dollar-for-dollar matching, so that housewives do not have to worry about their livelihood in old age.

sections.label: Women elected to Parliament
sections.summary: Women elected into Parliament rose from 3% in the First Parliament of 1965 to 23% in the current 13th Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In politics, the number of women who have been successfully elected into Parliament has risen from 3% in the First Parliament of 1965 to 23% in the current 13th Parliament.

sections.label: Women leaking from promotion pipeline
sections.summary: McKinsey & Co and Lean-In research found women leak out of the promotion pipeline mid-career, widening career gaps higher up the hierarchy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Research by McKinsey & Co and Lean-In has suggested that while there is an almost equal representation of women and men at entry-level jobs, women "leak" out of the promotion pipeline during the mid-career stage and the career gaps between women and men widen as one progresses further up the organisational hierarchy.

sections.label: HR fair promotion for women
sections.summary: HR departments need to advocate and arbitrate in promotion decisions so women are evaluated fairly on performance merit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: HR departments need to play the role of an advocate and arbitrator during promotion decisions and ensure that women are evaluated fairly and duly considered for promotion based on the merit of their performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I agree with Ms Tin Pei Ling that we need to move from an input model where the emphasis is placed on facetime in an office to an output model where the emphasis is placed on the quality of one's job performance.

sections.label: Shared parental and paternity leave
sections.summary: Recent changes to shared parental leave and paternity leave are positive but one can go beyond leave provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The recent changes to shared parental leave and paternity leave are a positive move in the right direction but can we go a little bit beyond leave provisions?

sections.label: SkillsFuture support for back-to-work moms
sections.summary: Asks whether SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce SG can create programmes and enhance SkillsFuture credit for back-to-work moms to upskill and reskill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce SG consider creating dedicated programmes to help back-to-work moms upskill and reskill themselves so that they can be relevant to the needs of the labour market?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can we enhance the SkillFuture credit scheme for moms so that they can take more market-relevant courses when they choose to return to work?

sections.label: e2i placement for back-to-work moms
sections.summary: Asks whether NTUC's e2i can have a dedicated placement programme pairing back-to-work moms with progressive companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) consider having a dedicated placement programme to help pair back-to-work moms with progressive companies that are willing to offer opportunities to these ladies?

sections.label: Expanded eldercare home and day care
sections.summary: States home care places grew from 3,800 in 2011 to around 7,500 today and day care from 2,100 to 4,000, targeting 10,000 and 6,200 by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: Ms Tin Pei Ling and Ms Joan Pereira asked that we provide more eldercare services and locate them in convenient locations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: We have expanded our home care capacity from 3,800 places in 2011 to around 7,500 home care places today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: We have also increased our day care places from 2,100 in 2011 to 4,000 today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: We are on target to grow this to 10,000 home care and 6,200 day care places by 2020.

sections.label: Caregivers' Training Grant subsidies
sections.summary: States subsidies of up to $200 per annum from the Caregivers' Training Grant are provided for caregivers, including foreign domestic workers, to attend caregiving or self-care courses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: Third, we are equipping our caregivers to provide better care for their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: We currently provide subsidies of up to $200 per annum from the Caregivers' Training Grant (CTG) for caregivers who are caring for seniors or those with a disability, including foreign domestic workers (FDWs), to attend training courses on caregiving or self-care skills.

sections.label: Eldercare leave not legislated yet
sections.summary: States the issue is being studied with unions and employers, and eldercare leave is not ready to be legislated now, balancing employer costs and manpower against caregivers' leave needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: We have been studying the issue in consultation with unions and employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: We are not ready to legislate eldercare leave at this time because we need to strike a balance between employers' concern on business costs and manpower constraints, and caregivers' need for more leave for eldercare purposes.

sections.label: OCBC family leave example
sections.summary: States OCBC offers two days of family leave for employees not entitled to childcare leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: For example, the Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) offers two days of family leave for employees who are not entitled to childcare leave.

sections.label: ART subsidies and egg freezing
sections.summary: A suggestion to extend ART subsidies and allow egg freezing was made, but there are no plans to extend ART subsidies to private centres now.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: He suggested measures, such as extending subsidies for ART, and allowing egg freezing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: We have no plans to extend ART subsidies to private centres at this point in time.

sections.label: ART live birth rates
sections.summary: From 2011 to 2015, the average live birth rate from ART was 20.7% at public centres and 19.8% at private centres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: From 2011 to 2015, the average live birth rate from ART was 20.7% at public centres, compared to 19.8% at private centres.

sections.label: Studying social egg freezing feasibility
sections.summary: The feasibility of allowing social egg freezing is currently being studied.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, we are currently studying the feasibility of allowing social egg freezing.

sections.label: Women's literacy rate in 1965
sections.summary: In 1965, the literacy rate for women was 43%, far behind men at 76%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In 1965, the literacy rate for women was a dismal 43%, far behind men at 76%.

sections.label: Employment rate for women aged 25-54
sections.summary: The employment rate for women aged 25-54 is currently 78%, a 10-percentage point increase from a decade ago, but lower than men at 92%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The employment rate for women aged 25-54 is currently 78%, a 10-percentage point increase from a decade ago, and high by international standards, but still lower than that of men at 92%.

sections.label: Median wage for women
sections.summary: Today, the median wage for women is 85% that of men.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, the median wage for women is 85% that of men.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Engage nationwide outreach
sections.summary: SSG will launch SkillsFuture Engage with PA, CDCs, Workforce Singapore and NTUC's e2i to guide individuals on career planning and training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Later this year, SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) will be launching a nationwide effort called SkillFuture Engage, where it will partner the People's Association (PA), the Community Development Councils (CDCs), Workforce Singapore, and NTUC's e2i to reach out to the community and guide individuals on career planning and identifying the right training programmes to acquire the relevant skills for employment.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit and programme subsidies
sections.summary: SkillsFuture Credit is a modest amount for Singaporeans, while $400 million of subsidies goes to selected programmes focused on industry skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: On the demand end, SkillsFuture Credit is a fairly modest amount given to every Singaporean to access a huge gamut of courses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But on the supply end is the $400 million of subsidies going to a few thousand programmes more sharply focused towards helping you get the skills to enter industry.

sections.label: Over-customisation risks stigmatising groups
sections.summary: Over-customising risks inadvertently stigmatising the very group being helped.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: When we over-customise, we run the risk of inadvertently stigmatising the very group that we are trying to help.

sections.label: Government or jobseeker customisation
sections.summary: Customisation can be by Government for specific groups or by jobseekers with guidance, such as packages for back-to-work women.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: One, by the Government, to cater to specific groups or demography; or, two, by the jobseeker himself or herself, with the right guidance and support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, within our dedicated effort to reach out to back-to-work women, we can identify and recommend a package of programmes which may be useful to jobseekers in their circumstances.

sections.label: Parliament spreading SkillsFuture message
sections.summary: Members of the House can spread the SkillsFuture message and guide individuals to the right channels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is where all of us in this House have a role to play.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We can all help to spread the message of SkillsFuture, looking out for individuals who could better benefit from our programmes and schemes, and guiding them to the right channels.

sections.label: Women in labour force 2016
sections.summary: Based on MOM's 2016 report, women make up 45.8% of Singapore's total labour force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, women take up 45.8% of our total labour force, based on MOM's report in 2016.

sections.label: Gender gap predictions and rankings
sections.summary: The World Economic Forum predicted in 2015 it would take 117 years to close the gender gap, and YouGov ranked Singapore 12th of 24 countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2015, the World Economic Forum predicted that it would take 117 years for women to completely fill the gender gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In that same year, YouGov released a report that saw Singapore ranking 12th in gender equality amongst 24 countries − behind China and Hong Kong.

sections.label: Young adults on male household heads
sections.summary: Among those aged 18-29, 66% of men believed men should be heads of households, compared to 43% of women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Of those aged 18-29, 66% of men believed that men should be heads of households, compared to only 43% of women in that age group.

sections.label: Paternity leave less than maternity leave
sections.summary: Paternity leave is much less than maternity leave, and adoption leave is available only to adoptive mothers, not adoptive fathers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One clear example is how there is much less paternity leave than maternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This extends even to adoption leave being available only to adoptive mothers and not adoptive fathers, though there is no biological argument about recovery from pregnancy and childbirth or breastfeeding which can justify this.

sections.label: Women under-represented on company boards
sections.summary: Women held only 9.5% of directorships in all SGX-listed companies as of 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is it also any surprise that women are under-represented on company boards, at only a mere 9.5% of directorships in all Singapore Exchange (SGX) listed companies as of 2015?

sections.label: Marital rape exemption in law
sections.summary: Laws exempt marital rape from the criminal offence of rape unless certain conditions are met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By that, I mean our laws that exempt marital rape from the criminal offence of rape unless certain conditions are met.

sections.label: Promoting early financial literacy
sections.summary: One proposal is that financial literacy should be promoted, and done early.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: One, we should promote financial literacy and do this early.

sections.label: CPF top-up retirement adequacy
sections.summary: Suggests incentivising women and family members to top up her CPF to the Basic Retirement Sum with dollar matching.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Two, there is a need to promote retirement adequacy and this could be done through the CPF scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: A woman and her family members should be further incentivised to top up her CPF account up to the Basic Retirement Sum by offering a certain amount of dollar matching for the top-ups made.

sections.label: SkillsFuture package for mature women
sections.summary: Proposes a specific SkillsFuture package for mature or retired women returning to work and acquiring skill certification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Three, a specific SkillsFuture package to be designed for mature or retired women who are seeking to return to work and in acquiring skill certification.

sections.label: Caregiving affects financial independence
sections.summary: States that a woman who stops working to care for children or parents has her financial independence and retirement preparation affected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: For instance, if a woman chooses to stop working to take care of her children or parents, her ability to be financially independent and prepare for retirement will be affected.

sections.label: CPF top-ups and SkillsFuture for women
sections.summary: Suggests incentives for topping up women's CPF accounts and SkillsFuture programmes for women who stopped working to care for family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is important, especially in an increasingly challenging world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I also suggest that incentives should be given to women and their family members for topping up the women's CPF account.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: If the top-up is supplemented by the Government, it will encourage women to want to reach a certain amount in their CPF accounts and this will at least ensure that she has money for her retirement, especially if she is not working and could not receive CPF contributions from an employer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In addition, I also hope for SkillsFuture programmes tailored specifically for women who have not worked for a while to take care of family members who do not require their care any longer, perhaps, because their parents have passed on and their children have all grown up.

sections.label: Female Members of Parliament today
sections.summary: Notes there are 21 female Members of Parliament, including a Minister, four Senior Ministers of State, one Parliamentary Secretary and two Mayors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Today, we have 21 female Members of Parliament and, amongst them, we have a Minister, four Senior Ministers of State and one Parliamentary Secretary, not to mention two Mayors, a Chairman of an opposition party and, of course, an enlightened and capable Speaker.

sections.label: Women on corporate boards
sections.summary: States that only one in 10 on corporate boards is a woman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Only one in 10 on our corporate boards is a woman.

sections.label: Robert Walters women leadership report
sections.summary: A Robert Walters report published last year stated that 75% of working women in Singapore feel inadequately represented in leadership positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In fact, recruitment specialist, Robert Walters, in a report that was published last year, stated that 75% of working women in Singapore feel that they are inadequately represented in leadership positions.

sections.label: Grants and tax reliefs for caregivers
sections.summary: The speaker repeats a call for stay-at-home-mothers and caregivers to receive the same grants and tax reliefs as working women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Often, it is women who are expected to take on these roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, firstly, I repeat my call made in previous speeches and echoed by many Members of this House for stay-at-home-mothers and caregivers to be provided the same grants and tax reliefs that working women are granted.

sections.label: Hays survey on gender equality
sections.summary: A Hays survey last month found 83% of men but only 63% of women saw pay equality, and 79% of men versus 65% of women saw meritocracy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Just last month, recruitment firm Hays conducted a survey and released the result on workplace gender equality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This report also pointed out a very large perception gap − 83% of Singapore men think that there is pay equality between men and women at their workplace, but only 63% of women in the same companies shared that view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Seventy-nine percent, in the same survey, of men believed that meritocracy already exists in career opportunities regardless of gender; for women, only 65% believed so.

sections.label: Survey on man provider woman carer
sections.summary: Close to 60% of those surveyed believed the best family arrangement is a man as provider and a woman as carer, versus 40% in the early 1990s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Close to 60% of those who were surveyed believed that the best family arrangement is where the man was provider and a woman was the carer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This contrasts with only 40% of respondents holding this view in the early 1990s.

sections.label: CDA and maternity leave for single mothers
sections.summary: The Child Development Account scheme and 16-week maternity leave were extended to children born out of wedlock and these single mothers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Child Development Account (CDA) scheme was extended to children born out of wedlock and the 16-week maternity leave was also extended to these single mothers, similar to other mothers.

sections.label: Single unwed mothers housing age rule
sections.summary: Single unwed mothers cannot buy a house under the family nucleus scheme, and most are under 35, so they do not meet the age requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For this group of people, they are not allowed to buy a house under the family nucleus scheme as children born out of wedlock are not regarded as part of a family nucleus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, a majority of these single unwed mothers are not even 35 years old, and, hence, do not fulfil this age requirement.

sections.label: Supporting Singapore women's aspirations
sections.summary: The House is asked to unanimously support a Motion affirming Singapore women in familial and career aspirations, including Muslim women wishing to use the tudung in nursing and uniformed vocations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We have heard spirited speeches from hon Members to convince the House to unanimously support the Motion that is being tabled, that is, to affirm and support Singapore women in fulfilling their familial and career aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope that Members in this House will not exclude Muslim women who wish to fulfil their career aspirations in line with their religious obligations, that is, allowing the use of the headscarf or tudung in the nursing and uniformed vocations, such as the Home Team and the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF).

sections.label: Women labour force participation rate
sections.summary: Women's labour force participation rate is 60.4%, with 40% of women not working, family care being the main reason for leaving the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With women labour force participation rate at 60.4%, 40% of women are not working, with family care being the main reason for dropping out of the workforce.

sections.label: Defraying flexible work arrangement costs
sections.summary: The Government is asked whether it can defray part of the increased cost of rolling out flexible work arrangements such as job-sharing so businesses are more willing to explore them permanently.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is the Government able to defray part of the increased cost of rolling out flexible work arrangements, such as job-sharing, so that businesses are more willing to embark on exploring the viability of such working arrangements on a more permanent basis?

sections.label: Returnship programme for women PMEs
sections.summary: NTUC called for Government support for women PMEs returning to work through a returnship programme, and the Government is asked to fund and recognise willing employers.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, the National Trades Union Congress made a call for the Government to support women PMEs who wish to return to the workforce after a period of absence through a returnship programme where companies take in women PMEs with work experience for three to six months to help them to assimilate back into the working world.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Government support enlightened employers who are willing to embark on the returnship programme through funding and recognition, and handhold them in guiding these women returnees?

sections.label: Women on boards target
sections.summary: On 24 March 2017, BoardAgender and the PAP Women's Wing called for an aspirational goal of at least 20% of women on boards of directors by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 24 March 2017, BoardAgender and People's Action Party Women's Wing called for the 2020 target setting of working towards having at least 20% of women on boards of directors by 2020 as an aspirational goal.

sections.label: Encouraging women in leadership
sections.summary: The Government is asked to encourage systematic inclusion of women in leadership through tertiary programmes and talent management, given the current 9.7% of women on boards.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What can the Government do to encourage a more systematic inclusion of women at various levels of leadership so that more women may take on top leadership positions or boards of director than the current 9.7%?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One way is to include programmes or curriculum in tertiary institutions that will allow women to have a mock experience.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While they are in employment, under talent management programmes, these women can be further identified and put through programmes that will enable them to further shine in their roles.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We need to have deliberate means of providing women with these opportunities if we want to see real progress in the next 50 years.

sections.label: Muslim women hijab, Workers' Party stance
sections.summary: Speaker says hijab is an obligation for Muslim women and that the Workers' Party does not oppose tudung, calling for dialogue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: As a Muslim husband and a father to a daughter, yes, it is an obligation for Muslim women to don hijab in whatever circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: In terms of the Party's stance on this, the Workers' Party had actually issued a statement sometime in November 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: The gist of the statement is that Workers' Party does not oppose wearing of tudung, but we call for more dialogues amongst the stakeholders as well as the larger community and it should be based on mutual understanding.

sections.label: Sensitive matters under closed-door review
sections.summary: Government and community leaders have been discussing sensitive matters in closed-door platforms, and the matter continues under review.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I am also a husband of my wife.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: That is why Government leaders and community leaders of all races and religions have been actively discussing such sensitive and deeply emotive matters in a number of closed-door platforms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: It is not easily resolved, considering all the moving parts on this matter, but I am glad it continues to be under review.

sections.label: Right way to discuss, madrasah progress
sections.summary: The speaker says there is a right time, place and way to discuss this, citing madrasah progress such as Edusave extension and fee waivers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: There is a right time, a right place and a right way to discuss this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This approach has achieved for the community progress in recent years, which includes the extension of Edusave to madrasah students in 2013, waiving national examination fees for secular subjects taken by madrasah students in 2015 and better supporting madrasah teachers who teach secular subjects from this year.

sections.label: High-profile championing and political points
sections.summary: The speaker says championing in a high-profile way and using it to score political points will not strengthen trust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Championing them in a high-profile way, which the Member does once in a while, using them to score political points, will not strengthen trust.

sections.label: Policies helping Malay families, Malay examples
sections.summary: The speaker says policies have helped Malay families in education, reskilling and rental flat ownership, naming Zuraidah Abdullah, Rahayu Buang and Fatimah Lateef.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Indeed, many of these policies have helped Malay families tangibly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We are putting our efforts in education, raising the levels of achievement, helping to retrain and reskill older Malays, and getting Malay families living in rental flats to own them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: One such example is Mdm Zuraidah Bte Abdullah, who is the Senior Assistant Commissioner of Police, the highest-ranking Senior Officer in the Police; Chairperson of the Malay Heritage Foundation and a member of the National Library Board.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Another is Ms Rahayu Binte Buang, CEO of MENDAKI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Yet another is our colleague, Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, a Senior Consultant at SGH Emergency Medicine.

sections.label: Strident approach and multi-racial harmony
sections.summary: The speaker tells Mr Faisal Manap that his strident approach is putting Singapore's multi-racial harmony at risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Perhaps, it is the spirit of the first world Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I put to Mr Faisal Manap that his strident approach is putting Singapore's multi-racial harmony at risk.

sections.label: Court fines imam offensive remarks
sections.summary: An imam was found guilty and fined for offensive remarks about Christians and Jews, while two others received stern warnings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Yesterday, the imam who made offensive remarks about Christians and Jews was found guilty by the Court and fined for the offensive remarks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Two others who traded barbs over the new media were given stern warnings.

sections.label: Racial and religious harmony tended
sections.summary: The speaker says harmony has been tended fastidiously and will not take Faisal Manap's tactic lightly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Yes, it is in a way, but it is because we have tended to our racial and religious harmony fastidiously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: And, therefore, I will not take Mr Faisal Manap's tactic lightly and let him needle the community's sensitivity subtly and frequently.

sections.label: Subtly raising sensitive community issues
sections.summary: The Member need not intend discord, but subtly and frequently raises sensitive issues, turning them into state-versus-religion matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The Member does not need to intend to sow discord.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: But the practice of subtly and frequently bringing issues that are sensitive to the community, knowing that these are not easy to resolve and cleverly turning it into a state-versus-religion issue.

sections.label: Government addresses sensitive matters privately
sections.summary: The Government addresses sensitive matters behind closed doors with community leaders rather than in public forums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The Government does not address this in public forums, in debates, in places like this where sensitive matters can be discussed out of context, emotionally and, sometimes, because they are not easy to resolve, because they cannot be quickly resolved, leaves a lingering, unhappy feeling in a community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: It may not be our community, it can be any community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Therefore, the approach of the Government is to address this within closed doors, with the community leaders and people who are responsible to carry the message for us and with us.

sections.label: Reserved Elected President and Malay position
sections.summary: The result was to proceed with the reserved Elected President, brushing aside the view that a Malay cannot assume the highest state position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: Again, the result was to proceed with the reserved Elected President based on, to brush aside the perspective that a Malay cannot assume the highest position in the state both by the Malays themselves as well as the non-Malays.

sections.label: Discussing sensitive issues quietly with Ministers
sections.summary: The speaker met Ministers to discuss the issue quietly, agreeing some things are discussed openly and not shared out there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Did I have to go out and go and try and create havoc?

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We do not need a place in Parliament to voice things out when we know that it is sensitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I met Ministers, Senior Ministers of State ─ at that time, it was Dr Aline Wong ─ to discuss the issue quietly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We had an agreement that there are things that we discuss here openly and do not share out there because there may be things that may be misunderstood and we have to move on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Because after that, the community leaders came together to calm the situation down and got everybody to move on.

sections.label: SkillsFuture returnship for women
sections.summary: SkillsFuture course packages and a three-to-six-month returnship programme can help back-to-work women with flexi-work or part-time arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To elaborate, under the SkillsFuture initiatives, specific course packages can be designed to help women in areas, such as information technology skills, effective use of social media, issues on cybersecurity, or even an overview of financial or social assistance schemes and policies that they need to know and can leverage on to help our women manage their multiple roles and responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This returnship programme can provide our back-to-work women with a flexi-work or part-time work arrangement in the first instance for a period of three to six months, before they decide to resume full-time work.

sections.label: Maternity and paternity leave changes
sections.summary: Mothers have 16 weeks maternity leave and two-week paternity leave started 1 January, helping couples share parenthood responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Changes to maternity leave provisions, where mothers have 16 weeks of maternity leave, and the introduction of the two-week paternity leave from 1 January this year have been significant in helping young couples share the joy and responsibilities of parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While I hope for greater provision of both maternity and paternity leave in future, as well as eldercare sick leave to be the norm, too, I recognise that shared responsibilities towards parenthood and the family are not just up to the Government to provide.

sections.label: Employers and eldercare leave
sections.summary: Support from government, professionals or helpers does not replace caregiving, so employers need to provide eldercare leave too.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government, geriatric professionals or domestic helpers can be there to lend support and assistance, but not to assume the entire role of caregiving to the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We would need employers to make provisions not just for maternity or paternity leave, but also for eldercare leave.

sections.label: Women's financial independence and participation
sections.summary: Women are increasingly financially independent, but with female labour participation around 60%, more economic activity is possible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am heartened by this, where our women are increasingly more financially independent and are able to earn their keep, without having to depend on their husbands or children or on others.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, with our labour participation rate for women at around 60%, there are many opportunities for our women to be even more economically active.

sections.label: Malay women not working
sections.summary: The proportion of Malay women who are not working is higher than in other communities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Having said that, however, the proportion of Malay women who are not working is higher, compared to the other communities in Singapore.

sections.label: Women's retirement adequacy planning
sections.summary: Women should plan for retirement adequacy, as they generally live longer and may need to support themselves in old age.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Furthermore, women should plan for retirement adequacy for the future when they grow old.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We have to recognise that, in general, women have longer life expectancies than men and a greater likelihood of having to support themselves and be financially independent even in their silver years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the six years I have served as a Member of Parliament, I have often encountered our Malay women residents who are quite elderly, that is, more than 65 years, who have no income or savings of their own, no spouse because their husbands have either died or they have divorced and may have also been abandoned by their children.

sections.label: Women on corporate boards
sections.summary: Minister Grace Fu cited a statistic that only 9.7% of board positions in Singapore corporates are held by women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: A statistic that Minister Grace Fu brought up recently is disturbing − only 9.7% of board positions in Singapore corporates are filled by women.

sections.label: Women community leaders numbers
sections.summary: Anecdotal evidence suggests women are about 40% of Resident's Committee leaders and about 20% or less of Citizens' Consultative Committee leaders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Anecdotal evidence suggests that women community leaders at the Resident's Committee level number about 40% but women community leaders at the Citizens' Consultative Committee level number about 20%, if not less.

sections.label: Women's employment after childbearing years
sections.summary: Minister Ong Ye Kung said the employment rate for women drops sharply after ages 25-29, coinciding with peak childbearing years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As Minister Ong Ye Kung pointed out yesterday, the employment rate for women shows a sharp drop after 25-29 years, which coincides with peak childbearing years.

sections.label: Childcare centres open till 8pm
sections.summary: The passage asks whether childcare centres could stay open until 8.00 pm so parents have time to pick up children after work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can we look at options to keep childcare centres open till 8.00 pm, so that parents have a reasonable amount of time to pick up their children after work?

sections.label: Training and flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: Considering women's needs and concerns, training or flexible work arrangements could help companies retain or re-employ female employees, with Industry Transformation Maps for HR practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In this area, if we could take into consideration their needs and concerns, we will be able to better support them by providing training or flexible work arrangement (FWA), so that companies can retain or re-employ female employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Just as we have Industry Transformation Maps for technology, there can be Industry Transformation Maps for HR practices.

sections.label: MOE childcare centres and hours
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOE could set up MOE childcare centres, not just MOE Kindergartens, and options to keep childcare centres open till 8.00 pm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Would it be possible for MOE to consider setting up MOE childcare centres instead of just MOE Kindergartens?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: When it comes to opening hours, what options are there to keep childcare centres open till 8.00 pm so that parents have a reasonable amount of time to travel to pick up their children?

sections.label: Caregiving support for working women
sections.summary: The speaker says paid and unpaid caregiving support enabled her to keep working, and calls for an inclusive, affordable caregiving ecosystem for all women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And I could only do what I do because I had supportive teams at work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I had state-subsidised infant care near my home, I had my mum and my sister taking turns being caregiver to my dad, and we could afford external part-time caregivers when my mom needed a break.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I love doing my work, but I know I would definitely have had to drop out of the workforce if I did not have access to an equal system of paid and unpaid help supporting me at the home level, as well as at the broader societal level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we want to see more women keep their families together, keep contributing to the economy and keep rising to represent us on corporate boards and political positions, we do have to design an inclusive ecosystem of caregiving that all women can access and afford.

sections.label: Caregiving driven by lack of capital
sections.summary: Some women become caregivers not by choice but because they lack financial capital for paid help or social capital for unpaid help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But for other women, it is not that simple.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They may share similar values as the first group and embrace the meaning of caregiving as well, but their decision to be a caregiver may be driven more out of a lack of financial capital to engage paid help or a lack of social capital to engage alternative sources of unpaid help.

sections.label: Women leaving labour force
sections.summary: MOM's 2015 report shows 80,848 women aged 25 to 54 left the labour force for family responsibilities, versus 4,439 men.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to MOM Report on the Labour Force in Singapore for 2015, 80,848 women between the ages of 25 and 54 left the labour force due to family responsibilities, compared to just 4,439 men.

sections.label: Singapore female labour force participation
sections.summary: Singapore's female labour force participation rate of 58.6% in 2014 was lower than Denmark's 75% and Switzerland's 79%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our female labour force participation rate of 58.6% in 2014 was lower than in most other first world countries at similar income levels, like Denmark at 75% and Switzerland at 79%.

sections.label: CPF transfers for caregivers
sections.summary: Voluntary incentivised CPF transfers exist, but with an estimated 210,000 caregivers, many still receive no CPF retirement savings for their work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, there is a system of voluntary CPF transfers from income-earners to non-earning caregivers that is incentivised by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But if we have an estimated 210,000 caregivers here, then it does imply that there are still many caregivers who do not receive CPF retirement savings for their work.

sections.label: Affordable childcare as employment barrier
sections.summary: Lack of affordable childcare blocks some women from finding or keeping jobs, and the speaker hopes to remove the employment requirement for women with household income below $2,500.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The barrier faced by some of these women in finding a job or keeping a job is, in fact, the lack of affordable childcare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope we can help them in their search for employment and removing the requirement of employment for women with household income lower than $2,500.

sections.label: Caregiving infrastructure for elderly, children, disabled
sections.summary: The speaker believes a caregiving infrastructure providing universal access to caregiving services for elderly, children and people with disabilities will have to be designed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given how fast our dependency ratio is rising and how much we need our women to stay in the workforce, I believe somewhere down the road, we will have to design a caregiving infrastructure that provides universal access to caregiving services for our elderly, children and people with disabilities.

sections.label: Ho Kwon Ping on female conscription
sections.summary: In 2015 Ho Kwon Ping proposed universal female conscription of three to five months in community care, supporting civil defence, Home Team and healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2015, Mr Ho Kwon Ping argued in his IPS-Nathan Lecture that we should consider universal female conscription as a solution to the overwhelming flood of future needs we will soon face in community care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: He proposed that while Singaporean men serve a two-year military regime, Singaporean women could serve a three- to five-month community conscription during their break between graduation and entering the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: He imagined female national service women as a force that could support our civil defence, Home Team community and healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: He believed that female national service women could really make a difference in service to their country's oldest, weakest and poorest, providing support in caregiver relief, elder care or even childcare while lessening our dependence on foreign caregivers.

sections.label: Women's Charter passed in 1961
sections.summary: The Women's Charter was passed in 1961, two years after the PAP came into power and before Singapore's Independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Women's Charter was passed in 1961, barely two years after the PAP came into power and even before Singapore's Independence.

sections.label: Male and female workforce participation
sections.summary: In the 30s, male workforce participation spikes from about 89% to 98%, whereas female workforce participation drops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the 20s, it is about the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But in the 30s, male workforce participation spikes from about 89% to 98%, whereas female workforce participation drops.

sections.label: Women's Wing flexible work position
sections.summary: The Women's Wing had said in 2013 flexible work should be mandated as a legal right, but has instead recommended a tripartite workgroup arrangement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Women's Wing had previously taken a stronger position in 2013, saying that flexible work should be mandated; it should be made a legal right that employers have to observe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What it has actually recommended instead is a tripartite arrangement − a tripartite workgroup to look into creating flexible work arrangements within industries.

sections.label: Fairer workplace appraisal system
sections.summary: Workplace appraisals sometimes depend on face-time, but a fairer system should appraise people on work quality, not time in office or childcare leave taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is a tendency observed that workplace appraisals sometimes depend a great deal on face-time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, a fairer appraisal system should find ways to make sure that people are appraised on the quality of their work and not just the amount of time they spend at the office or the amount of say, childcare leave they take.

sections.label: Women's Wing subsidised courses suggestion
sections.summary: The Women's Wing suggested subsidised courses in areas of interest to women to develop skills for returning to the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
