sentences.text: The Women's Wing suggestion was for subsidised courses in areas of interest to women where they could develop skills to assimilate themselves back into the workforce.

sections.label: Study on gender and ethnic diversity
sections.summary: A study of London companies found top-quartile gender diversity performed 15% better on return on equity and ethnic diversity 35% better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This study talked about diversity in two respects: gender diversity and ethnic diversity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It was a study of companies in London and what it found was that companies at the top quartile for gender diversity, performed 15% better on a return on equity basis than other companies, while companies with the top quartile for ethnic diversity performed 35% better.

sections.label: Women's Wing SGX representation proposal
sections.summary: The Women's Wing paper suggested SGX require at least 20% women representation in all companies by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Women's Wing paper has suggested that the SGX put some kind of requirements in place to ensure we have at least 20% representation of women in all companies by 2020.

sections.label: Women in parliaments and Singapore politics
sections.summary: In 2013 women were 21% of parliamentarians worldwide, and Singapore had one woman among 20 full Cabinet Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to the United Nations, although women can vote and run for public office in nearly every country, in 2013, they accounted for only 21% of parliamentarians worldwide and serve as Head of State or Head of Government in only 24 countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Singapore, as many of us have said, we only have one woman among 20 full Cabinet Ministers and about 20% of Members of Parliament are women.

sections.label: CEDAW on women's participation impact
sections.summary: CEDAW stated women's participation reaching 30% to 35% impacts political style and decisions, and active measures are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women had stated that, "Research demonstrates that if women's participation reaches 30% to 35%, there is a real impact on political style and the content of decisions, and political life is revitalised." The General Recommendation essentially emphasises that it is not enough to say there is no formal barrier − active measures should be taken to substantially ensure equal participation.

sections.label: Women out of labour force
sections.summary: MOM figures show over 265,000 women are out of the labour force due to family commitments, versus around 9,000 men.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to MOM, over 265,000 women are out of the labour force due to family commitments or responsibilities, versus around 9,000 men.

sections.label: AWARE and Diversity Action Committee
sections.summary: The speaker notes AWARE's efforts to support women and urges businesses to connect with AWARE and the Diversity Action Committee to assist women employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I also note the efforts by AWARE which has constantly sought to support women from all walks of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I urge businesses and organisations to connect with them and the Diversity Action Committee to find out how they may assist their women employees.

sections.label: Speaker's personal reasons for women's aspirations
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore women's aspirations matter personally, citing three daughters, and that it is the right thing to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The aspirations of Singapore women are clearly very important to me on a very personal note.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I have three daughters and I hope that they will be able to fulfil their family and career aspirations and to be future-ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But beyond these personal reasons, this is important to me quite simply because it is the right thing to do.

sections.label: Progress to number 12
sections.summary: Last year, the ranking progressed to number 12, just outside the top 10.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Last year, we progressed to number 12, just outside the top 10.

sections.label: CPF balances and flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: Average CPF balance for women grew 8.3% yearly over 10 years, and employees in companies offering flexible work arrangements rose from 56% to 67%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Thirdly, in terms of retirement adequacy, the average CPF balance for women has grown by 8.3% per year over the last 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Fourthly, the proportion of employees who work in companies offering flexible work arrangement has grown from 56% five years ago to 67% last year.

sections.label: Spouses' transfers increase
sections.summary: Last year saw 70% more cases of spouses' transfers totalling $110 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Last year, we saw 70% more cases of spouses' transfers totalling $110 million.

sections.label: Spousal transfers and Silver Support
sections.summary: The measure aims to help more spouses reach the basic Retirement Sum and participate in CPF LIFE, and Silver Support was introduced for bottom 20% of seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: This will enable more spouses to attain at least the basic Retirement Sum, which is our objective, to encourage more of such transfers so that more women will be able to have at least the basic Retirement Sum in their CPF savings so that they, too, can participate fully in the CPF LIFE scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We have also introduced Silver Support last year for the bottom 20% of seniors who had low pay, low wages or no wages throughout their lifetime and currently have little or no family support.

sections.label: Tripartite standards on flexible work
sections.summary: Tripartite partners will launch tripartite standards, including one on flexible work arrangements, to spread progressive workplace practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: As announced at MOM's Committee of Supply this year, the tripartite partners will be launching a series of tripartite standards to spread this public adoption of progressive workplace practices and flexible work arrangements will be one of them.

sections.label: Supporting women in schemes
sections.summary: Focus will be sharpened on supporting women in the Adapt and Grow initiative and CPF schemes, so women need not choose between family and career.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: At the same time, we will also sharpen our focus on supporting women in the implementation of the Adapt and Grow initiative and various CPF schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Women should not have to choose between family and career.

sections.label: Women's Charter passed in 1961
sections.summary: In 1961, the Women's Charter was passed as legislation to protect and advance the rights of women and girls.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: In 1961, we passed the Women's Charter' a seminal legislation to protect and advance the rights of women and girls.

sections.label: Women's literacy and employment rates
sections.summary: The literacy rate for women is 95.4%, and full-time employment for women aged 25 to 64 rose from 63% to 72%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: In a recent dialogue with Chinese journalist Yang Lan in February, I highlighted that our literacy rate for women is 95.4%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Our full-time employment rate for women aged 25 to 64 has increased from 63% 10 years ago to 72% last year.

sections.label: UN Gender Inequality Index ranking
sections.summary: The latest UN 2016 Human Development Report ranked Singapore 11th out of 159 countries on the UN Gender Inequality Index.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: In terms of gender equality, the latest UN 2016 Human Development Report ranked Singapore 11th out of 159 countries on the UN Gender Inequality Index.

sections.label: Increase in childcare places
sections.summary: Since 2012, childcare places increased by more than 40% to about 140,000, with another 10,000 to be added by early next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Since 2012, the number of childcare places has increased by more than 40% to about 140,000 places.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We will add another 10,000 childcare places by early next year.

sections.label: Childcare centres in commercial buildings
sections.summary: Last year, 450 childcare centres were located in or near commercial and Government buildings, about one-third of all childcare centres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Last year, there were 450 childcare centres located in or near commercial and Government buildings − that is about one-third of all childcare centres.

sections.label: Women in senior management and boards
sections.summary: Women hold about 21% of senior management roles in Singapore, similar to Australia, the US and the UK, but about 9.9% of board seats as of December 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The proportion of women in senior management roles in Singapore is about 21% − similar to other countries like Australia, the US and the UK.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Yet, women's representation on our boards is about 9.9% as of December 2016, which is really less than half the representation rate in these countries.

sections.label: Target for women directorships
sections.summary: Minister Grace Fu announced an ambition for at least 20% of directorships on SGX-listed companies to be held by qualified women by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Minister Grace Fu recently announced a declared ambition for at least 20% of directorships on SGX-listed companies to be held by qualified women by 2020.

sections.label: DAC multi-tiered board targets
sections.summary: For SGX-listed companies, DAC suggests targets of 20% by 2020, 25% by 2025 and 30% by 2030 for women on boards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: For SGX-listed companies, DAC is suggesting a multi-tiered target: 20% by 2020, 25% by 2025 and 30% by 2030 because getting women on boards is a journey and not a destination.

sections.label: Maternity leave and CDA for unwed mothers
sections.summary: The full 16-week maternity leave was recently extended to unwed mothers, and their children are now eligible for a Child Development Account.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: For example, we have recently extended the full 16-week maternity leave to unwed mothers and their children are now eligible for a Child Development Account (CDA).

sections.label: Review of marital immunity for rape
sections.summary: Married women should have the same access to protection as unmarried women, and the issue of marital immunity for rape is being actively reviewed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Married women should have the same access to protection as unmarried women.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We are thus actively reviewing the issue of marital immunity for rape and will give an update once the review is completed.

sections.label: Marriage and Parenthood study findings
sections.summary: A 2012 study found 99% agreed fathers and mothers are equally important caregivers, though chores and childcare mostly fall on women.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The 2012 Marriage and Parenthood study showed 99% of respondents, both men and women, either strongly agreed or agreed that "Fathers and mothers are equally important as caregivers for children." However, in terms of division of labour within the household, day-to-day chores and childcare responsibilities mostly still fall on the women's shoulders.

sections.label: Paternity leave and infantcare leave
sections.summary: Fathers are urged to use two weeks of mandatory paternity leave, and public servants get four weeks unpaid infantcare leave per parent from July.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: So, as much as is possible, we should start bonding with our children from birth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: So, I urge fathers, please use the two weeks of paternity leave which have been made mandatory from this year and be present in the lives of your children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: During the Committee of Supply debate a few weeks ago, Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo announced that, from July this year, public servants will get an additional four weeks of unpaid infantcare leave per parent, as part of a three-year pilot.

sections.label: Bosses on work-life initiatives
sections.summary: Over 80% of 500 bosses polled said work-life initiatives are important to improve satisfaction, raise productivity and retain talent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Of the 500 bosses polled, over 80% said they felt work-life initiatives are important to improve employee satisfaction, raise productivity and retain talent.

sections.label: Changing attitudes and home responsibilities
sections.summary: Attitudes are changing, but home responsibilities are disproportionately borne by women.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Attitudes are changing and that is encouraging and home responsibilities, unfortunately, are disproportionately borne by women.

sections.label: Considering Members' recommendations
sections.summary: The many useful and insightful recommendations Members put forth over two days will be seriously considered.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: In this regard, we will seriously consider the many useful and insightful recommendations that Members have put forth these two days.

sections.label: Removing glass ceilings for women
sections.summary: All have a stake in removing glass ceilings and giving Singaporean women the opportunity to achieve their fullest potential.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: All of us have a stake, whether as employers or colleagues in the workplace, as civil society or as families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We must remove glass ceilings and give Singaporean women − our mothers or sisters, our wives or daughters − the opportunity to achieve their fullest potential.

sections.label: Two-day debate on women's progress
sections.summary: Two days of debate showed women have made progress, but areas remain where the nation can take concrete steps to help women's aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We have had two days of robust debate and it is clear that women have made significant progress over the decades.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But that 18 Members of Parliament and five Ministers spoke over two days, it is also clear that there are still areas in which the nation can take pragmatic, concrete steps towards helping women achieve their aspirations, thereby benefiting families, increasing social capital and economic prosperity, and contributing to Singapore's long-term success.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements recommended
sections.summary: Speakers recommended flexible work arrangements so women need not sacrifice careers or feel guilty juggling roles, supported by many named Members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Those with career aspirations do not have to feel that they have to sacrifice or make trade-offs or even feel guilty about having to juggle two different roles and feel inadequate at any one point in time; or even for women who choose to want to focus their energy on their families, where their heart lies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And so, over the course of the two-day debate, we have made several recommendations, one of which is highly supported by almost all our speakers − flexible work arrangements − and this is echoed very passionately by our hon Members Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar, Ms Sun Xueling, Mr Vikram Nair, Miss Cheryl Chan, Mr Louis Ng and a few others.

sections.label: CPF top-ups for caregiving women
sections.summary: Several Members spoke about topping up the CPF of women who gave up careers to stay home and care for family members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: So, how can we help women who choose this path to free up their capacity, to free up their minds, so that they can focus on family caregiving a little bit more?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This is where several Members, such as Ms Joan Pereira, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Ms Rahayu Mahzam, Mr Alex Yam, Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar as well as Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin, have all talked about and, that is, to top up the CPF of women who have given up their careers to stay at home to care for their family members.

sections.label: Future-ready strategy for smart women
sections.summary: The fourth strategy is to be future-ready, to have smart women for a smart nation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The fourth strategy is to be future-ready, something that I feel very passionately about, to have smart women for a smart nation.

sections.label: Digital fluency as critical enabler
sections.summary: Digital fluency is a critical success factor and enabler for future jobs and balancing roles using smart solutions, echoed by Mr Darryl David.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This is something that is echoed by Mr Darryl David.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But underlying this, to enable both the future jobs as well as taking on the future jobs and being able to balance the different roles using smart solutions, digital fluency is a very critical success factor and a critical enabler.

sections.label: MOH looking into social egg freezing
sections.summary: MOH will look into social egg freezing, which concerns many couples wanting to raise healthy children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Of course, I am also heartened that MOH will be looking into social egg freezing, something that has been weighing on the minds of many couples who are concerned about their own future, their own families and wanting to raise healthy children.

sections.label: Women's Wing flexi-work and board representation
sections.summary: The speaker cites the PAP Women's Wing position paper on flexi-work standards and welcomes support for childcare near workplaces and 20% female board representation by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In fact, for the PAP Women's Wing last year, in our position paper, we also talked about something very similar in concept, the industry's specific flexi-work arrangement standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And the Minister also mentioned that the Adapt and Grow scheme will be customised for back-to-work women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We thank Minister Tan Chuan-Jin for also taking the lead and talking about how women are equals in this society, that we need to eliminate barriers at work and in the community, that we need to recognise the evolving roles between men and women at home, that we need to also take care of our vulnerable women and that there is a need to look into the changing and reshaping of attitudes towards women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I am definitely very heartened to hear that ECDA will be working with URA to bring childcare facilities nearer to workplaces and that the Minister expressed his explicit support for our aspiration of 2020 − 20% female representation on boards by the year 2020.

sections.label: Motion on women's strengths and gaps
sections.summary: The speaker says the Motion aims to build on women's strengths, close gaps, and make Singapore the best home for everyone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Again, my colleagues and I have moved this Motion with the aim of building on the strengths of women, to recognise and close the gaps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And most importantly, we desire to make Singapore the best home for everyone − a home where regardless of background or gender, Singaporeans have the capability, the opportunity and the courage to pursue our family and career aspirations and to lead a full and happy life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As Singapore is transforming to be future-ready, we − as Members of this House and certainly the whole of Singapore − should also ride on the momentum and translate our words into real action.
